concerns.text: Edge case 'semantic embeddings are ambiguous or fail to map to a unique discrete state... flag for manual review' has NO backing FR. FR-001/FR-002 cover conversion and mapping but neither requires ambiguity detection, graceful handling of non-unique mappings, or a manual-review flag. Add an FR (e.g., FR-011) anchored to this edge case, or fold the handling requirement into FR-002.

Edge case 'real-world execution failures mid-sequence... attempt to replan from the last known valid state if the policy supports it' is only partially covered. FR-006 covers failure logging/labeling but no FR requires mid-sequence replanning-from-last-valid-state behavior. Either add an FR for replan-on-failure or explicitly scope it out in the edge case.

US-2 scenario 2 requires a completion-rate report for all 18 tasks within ≤ 4 hours total wall-clock, but no SC measures end-to-end execution wall-clock (SC-002 measures only action-sequence generation time). Add an SC anchored to US-2 for the 4-hour execution-report bound, or note it is covered by an existing SC explicitly.

The spec defines the 'Perfect Low-Level Executor' (Oracle) as 'approximated by a high-fidelity simulation with ground-truth physics' (Assumptions), while FR-002 explicitly excludes 'continuous physics dynamics' from the SymbolicState and Constitution Principle VI mandates evaluation be 'strictly decoupled from continuous physics fidelity.' Using a physics-based oracle to compute the 'Physics Fidelity Gap' (SC-006) contradicts the spec's own abstraction premise and the constitution. Redefine the Oracle as a deterministic, non-physics rule-based verifier of the symbolic sequence against the ground-truth task graph.

FR-008 (ablation study mode) is anchored '(See US-3)', but none of US-3's acceptance scenarios mention varying state-representation detail; the ablation concept appears nowhere in any user story. Either add an acceptance scenario to US-3 (or a dedicated story) or re-anchor FR-008 so the cross-reference resolves to actual coverage.

SC-005 ('catastrophic failures ... ≤ 5%') is anchored to US-3, but no US-3 acceptance scenario and no FR defines or computes a 'catastrophic failure rate' (FR-006 only logs per-failure modes). The criterion is internally unanchored — add an FR/scenario defining how the rate is computed, or remove/re-anchor SC-005.

Terminology drift on the planner input: US-1 and FR-001/FR-002 describe the pipeline as task specification → semantic embeddings → SymbolicState, while FR-003 says the planner generates sub-goals 'based on abstract task descriptions.' Pick one term (e.g., 'SymbolicState graph derived from semantic embeddings') so the planner's input is consistently named.

SC-002 (wall-clock time to generate action sequences) is anchored '(See US-3)' but planning-time measurement belongs to US-1 (≤60s per plan on CPU); US-3 covers statistical comparison. Re-anchor to US-1.

SC-005 sets a catastrophic-failure threshold of ≤ 5%, but the evaluation domain is 18 tasks (US-2). One catastrophic failure = 5.6% > 5%, so the criterion is only satisfiable by zero failures. State the criterion in count terms over the 18-task domain (e.g., '≤ 1 of 18 tasks') or define the denominator/repetition count so the threshold is reachable and decidable.

SC-002 and FR-007 require comparison against 'the GPU-based baseline time' / 'GPU-based baseline' compute metrics, but the spec never states where the baseline's CPU-cycle/memory/wall-clock numbers come from. The project runs on CPU-only GitHub Actions runners (Constitution VII, US-1). Name the source of baseline compute measurements (published RoboDojo benchmark numbers, or a documented re-measurement procedure) so the percentage reduction is computable and reproducible.

'System must handle non-unique mappings gracefully or flag for manual review' is not verifiable — 'gracefully' and 'manual review' are undefined behaviors. Specify the observable output (e.g., a logged 'AmbiguousMapping' label with the candidate states, and the task marked as skipped/failed with that label) so the edge case can be confirmed met-or-not.

'attempt to replan from the last known valid state if the policy supports it, or record as a hard failure' leaves the behavior conditional on an unspecified capability. For testability, state which behavior the delivered system MUST exhibit (e.g., always log failure point + label, and record replan-attempt outcome as a logged field), so a test can decide pass/fail deterministically.

The spec's stated input question is 'can topological symbolic abstractions alone suffice to bridge the sim-to-real gap in generalist policies?' — but the source idea's research question is 'To what extent do topological task constraints versus continuous physical dynamics INDEPENDENTLY contribute to failure modes... REGARDLESS of the specific planning architecture?' The spec has silently redefined the question from factor-attribution (which factor is the bottleneck) to architecture-sufficiency (can our symbolic planner work). This is drift toward an easier, different question.

The idea's 'regardless of planning architecture' framing requires isolating the planning variable on BOTH sides. The spec compares only (Symbolic+Real) vs (Neural+Real) plus a (Symbolic+Oracle) control. There is no Neural+Oracle (or baseline-planning-isolation) control, so the spec cannot attribute the Neural baseline's failures to physics vs planning — exactly the attribution the idea demands. Under-reach relative to the idea's core question.

'The Perfect Low-Level Executor (Oracle) can be approximated by a high-fidelity simulation with ground-truth physics' directly contradicts Constitution Principle VI (evaluation strictly decoupled from continuous physics fidelity) and re-introduces the confound the idea is designed to isolate. The Oracle must be a non-physics rule-based verifier of the symbolic sequence against the ground-truth task graph.

No power/sample-size analysis for the Wilcoxon test over 18 paired tasks. With N=18 the test detects only massive effects; the idea's claim ('empirically quantify which factor is the primary limiting resource') cannot be supported without acknowledging/handling low power (e.g., effect-size reporting, exact test, or power analysis). This is essential rigor, not over-reach.

The idea's methodology depends on mapping continuous embeddings to discrete predicates; the spec's own edge case admits mappings may be 'ambiguous or non-unique', yet no FR requires measuring/validating mapping accuracy. Without it, 'Planner Infeasibility' (FR-006) is confounded by encoder error — under-reach on a component the idea's causal claim requires.

'A subset of the simulation tasks, the real-world RoboDojo tasks are used specifically for real-world validation' is garbled and drops the idea's 42 simulation task specifications from the data scope. Clarify which of the 42 sim tasks feed the planner (US-1 mentions '18 distinct RoboDojo tasks' for planning) and how this maps to the idea's data acquisition step.

The 'Perfect Low-Level Executor' is defined as 'a high-fidelity simulation with ground-truth physics'. This is causally circular for the hypothesis under test: the Oracle embodies exactly the continuous physics fidelity the project claims is unnecessary, so the 'Physics Fidelity Gap' (SC-006) conflates planner logic with physics-engine fidelity and violates Constitution Principle VI (metrics must be decoupled from physics fidelity). Replace with a deterministic, non-physics rule-based verifier of symbolic-sequence validity against the ground-truth task graph.

Wilcoxon signed-rank on 18 paired binary outcomes is statistically ill-suited: with binary per-task outcomes the test degenerates toward a sign test, discards effect-size information, and has very low power at N=18 (no power analysis or multiple-trials-per-task design is specified). Either run multiple execution trials per task to obtain graded success rates, or use an exact paired test for binary data (e.g., McNemar/exact binomial on discordant pairs) with an explicit power statement.

The Symbolic-vs-Neural comparison confounds the symbolic abstraction variable with the low-level controller adaptation (FR-009): the symbolic system uses an adapted controller while the baseline uses the original policy, and no 'Neural+Oracle' control exists, so failure attribution between planning and execution cannot be isolated for the baseline. The spec should either restrict the claim to system-level comparison or add the missing control condition.

The embedding→SymbolicState mapping is treated as deterministic, but it is a noisy perception step. No requirement validates mapping accuracy (e.g., predicate-level precision/recall against annotated ground truth), so 'Planner Infeasibility' failures (FR-006) are confounded with encoder/mapping errors. Add an FR measuring mapping accuracy independently of planner outcomes.

new_concerns.text: Functional Requirement FR-013 (precision and recall of the embedding‑to‑SymbolicState mapping) is not anchored to any user story or acceptance scenario. No story explicitly requires evaluation of mapping accuracy, so FR-013 is an orphan FR. Anchor it to User Story 1 (e.g., add a clause that the system MUST report precision/recall of the mapping) or remove it.

Functional Requirement FR-017 (obtain baseline GPU‑based compute metrics) lacks a clear trace to any user story or success criterion. Without an anchor, FR-017 is an orphan FR. Link it to a story (e.g., User Story 1 or 3) that demands compute‑overhead comparison, or delete it.
FR-014 references SC-012, which is not defined anywhere in the specification, creating an unresolved cross‑reference.
